headline: Fed holds with two hike dissents; memory chips lift the S&P 0.3% as Micron jumps 5.9%
summary: A quiet, narrow up day around the Fed. The major indexes hovered near unchanged before and after the 2 p.m. decision, swung during Chair Warsh's press conference and closed modestly higher, with the VIX easing to 16.91. Tech, financials and energy led while utilities, real estate and staples fell; the equal-weight S&P 500 finished flat, NYSE breadth was roughly even and Nasdaq advancers beat decliners about 1.5 to 1.
drivers: Fed holds, but the hawks are louder

The Fed kept rates at 3.75–4% in a 10–2 vote, with Governor Cook and Cleveland Fed President Hammack dissenting for a quarter-point hike; the statement upgraded the economy, called inflation still elevated and said it will deliver price stability. Warsh gave no forward guidance and said meetings will drop to seven next year; the curve steepened as the 2-year yield slipped about 3bp to 4.71% while the 10-year rose 3bp to 5.02%, and December hike odds climbed to about 85% from 78%.
SK hynix blowout fuels the memory trade

SK hynix said quarterly operating profit jumped more than sevenfold to 83.3 trillion won and that demand should outrun supply through 2030; its US-listed shares rose 13.3% and Micron 5.9%, the biggest single lift to the S&P 500. Arm gained about 4% and AMD and Marvell about 3%, taking the SOX up 1.8% for a fourth straight gain and tech to the top of the sector table (+0.8%).
Oil back above $100 on a Saudi refinery strike

Yemen's Houthis claimed a missile hit on Saudi Arabia's 550,000-barrel-a-day Ras Tanura refinery, and WTI rose 2.9% to $102.78, reversing Tuesday's drop; Iranian talk of giving diplomacy a chance trimmed the highs. Energy stocks were among the leaders and higher crude added to the upward pressure on long-dated yields.
Earnings: Vertiv soars, Alphabet sinks late

Vertiv jumped 16.5% after beating and raising its outlook, GE HealthCare rose 6.6% and Wendy's 15.1% on a Trian buyout offer, while Boston Scientific fell 5.8% on a soft forecast and Robinhood 3.3% on a profit miss. After the bell Microsoft rose about 2–4% on Azure revenue of $33.2 billion, but Alphabet fell about 8% on a revenue miss and its first-ever negative free cash flow (−$9.1 billion) as AI spending surged.
week: Three days into the week the S&P 500 is up 1.6%, the Nasdaq 2.3%, the Russell 2000 2.0% and the Dow 0.5%, leaving the S&P 500 about 0.9% below its Oct 5 record of 7,811.54; the backdrop is a 10-year yield above 5%, oil above $100 and a Fed leaning toward a December hike.
watch: Next: Thursday Oct 29 brings PCE inflation and the first Q3 GDP estimate plus the ECB decision, the market's first reaction to Alphabet and Microsoft, and earnings from Amazon, Intel, Samsung, Eli Lilly, Mastercard and Caterpillar, ahead of the Nov 3 midterms.
